'''''Eucomis''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Asparagaceae, subfamily Scilloideae, native to southern [[Africa]].<ref name=POWO/> Most species of this genus are commonly referred to as '''pineapple flowers''' or '''pineapple lilies'''. They are [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]]s with basal rosettes of leaves and stout stems covered in star-shaped flowers with a tuft of green [[bract]]s at the top, superficially resembling a pineapple – hence the common names.<ref name=RHSAZ/>

==Taxonomy==
The genus ''Eucomis'' was first published by [[Charles Louis L'Héritier de Brutelle|Charles L'Héritier]] in 1789.<ref name=POWO/><ref name=LHer89/> The name ''Eucomis'' is of Greek origin, ''eu-'' meaning "pleasing" and ''kome'' "hair of the head",<ref name=Coom94p70/> thus referring to the tuft of leaf-like [[bract]]s that crown the [[inflorescence]] of the species in this genus. The name was first used by [[Daniel Solander]], who decided that [[Carl Linnaeus|Linnaeus's]] ''Fritillaria regia'' should be placed in a separate genus. However, Solander died before publishing the name, and was not mentioned by L'Héritier in his 1789 publication.<ref name=Comp90/> Initially, three species were placed in ''Eucomis'': ''[[Eucomis regia|E. regia]]'', ''E. nana'' and ''E. punctata''.<ref name=LHer89/> (The last two are now [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]]s of ''E. regia''<ref name="POWO E.nana"/> and ''E. comosa''<ref name="POWO E.punctata"/> respectively.)

===Classification===
''Eucomis'' is placed in the subfamily [[Scilloideae]] of the family [[Asparagaceae]] by those who use the [[APG IV system|APG system]] of plant classification,<ref name=ChasReveFay09/> and in the family Hyacinthaceae by those who use more narrowly defined families.<ref name=MannGoldFay04/> Using the subfamily Scilloideae, ''Eucomis'' is placed in the tribe Hyacintheae, subtribe Massoniinae, along with such genera as ''[[Lachenalia]]'', ''[[Ledebouria]]'', ''[[Massonia]]'' and ''[[Veltheimia]]''.<ref name=PfosWetsUngaPren04/>

The species can be divided into two groups. One consists of seven mainly short, [[diploid]] species with 2''n'' = 2''x'' = 30 [[chromosome]]s: ''E. amaryllidifolia'', ''E. bicolor'', ''E. grimshawii'', ''E. regia'', ''E. schijffii'', ''E. vandermerwei'' and ''E. zambesiaca''. The other consists of five mainly larger, [[tetraploid]] species with 2''n'' = 4''x'' = 60 chromosomes: ''E. autumnalis'', ''E. comosa'', ''E. humilis'', ''E. montana'' and ''E. pallidiflora''.<ref name=ZonnDunc10/> The ploidy of ''E. sonnetteana'' is not known.<ref name=Fl.Pl.Africa/>

==Distribution and habitat==

''Eucomis'' is [[native plant|native]] to [[South Africa]], [[Botswana]], [[Lesotho]], [[Eswatini]], [[Zimbabwe]] and [[Malawi]]. Species can be found in grassland, forest, swamps and on river banks, but are absent from the drier regions.<ref name=PlantZAfrica/> The smaller species are more often found at higher elevations, on hilltops or other exposed places; the larger species favour less exposed habitats, such as damp gulleys and streamsides.<ref name=Comp90/>

==Cultivation==
''Eucomis'' species are cultivated as [[ornamental plant]]s. Most of the summer-flowering species will tolerate frost down to {{cvt|-5|to|-10|C|F}} when dormant in winter, provided they are kept dry. They flower best if given both sun exposure and moisture in summer.<ref name=Comp90/><ref name=PlantZAfrica/> ''Eucomis regia'' grows in winter and flowers in early spring. It needs [[greenhouse]] cultivation in regions that, like Britain, have a maritime rather than a Mediterranean climate.<ref name=Comp90/>
